answer: A seat lasts only while its table stays in memory. The table is a sonnet: 14 key-unique blocks of 256 MiB that cannot be shared or paged out. At an unpredictable moment the chain starts a gale, a 5-second burst that names one random offset in every block. The seat must return all 14 values, signed, as its pulse before the burst ends. Reloading a parked table misses that deadline, so 500 fakes occupy 1,750 GiB of live memory for the whole epoch, whether or not anyone later checks.
